title: Asado del domingo en San Telmo

dialogue.speaker: Martín
dialogue.spanish: Che, Flor, mirá qué suerte: acá en la carnicería del mercado queda el último kilo de vacío para el asado.
dialogue.english: Hey, Flor, look how lucky: right here at the market butcher shop they have the last kilo of flank steak for the barbecue.

dialogue.speaker: Flor
dialogue.spanish: ¡Qué joya! Bueno, llevate también cuatro chorizos criollos y una bolsa grande de carbón antes de que se acabe.
dialogue.english: What a gem! Well, grab four sausages and a big bag of charcoal too before it sells out.

dialogue.speaker: Martín
dialogue.spanish: Dale, el carnicero dice que son doce mil mangos en total por la carne y el carbón.
dialogue.english: Sounds good, the butcher says it's twelve thousand pesos total for the meat and charcoal.

slang.actualMeaning: bucks / pesos (classic Argentine slang for money)
slang.example: Esta campera me salió veinte mil mangos.

dialogue.speaker: Flor
dialogue.spanish: O sea, está re bien. ¿Ponemos mitad y mitad ahora o preferís que yo compre las bebidas?
dialogue.english: I mean, that's really good. Should we split it fifty-fifty now or do you prefer I buy the drinks?

dialogue.speaker: Martín
dialogue.spanish: Mejor comprá vos el vino tinto, el pan francés y los tomates para la ensalada en la verdulería.
dialogue.english: Better yet, you buy the red wine, French bread, and tomatoes for the salad at the produce stand.

dialogue.speaker: Flor
dialogue.spanish: De una, yo me encargo de eso acá al lado. ¡Nos va a quedar re copado el almuerzo en la terraza!
dialogue.english: Deal, I'll take care of that right next door. Lunch on the rooftop is going to turn out super cool!

slang.example: El lugar nuevo en Palermo está re copado.

questions.question: What items do Martín and Flor buy at the butcher shop for Sunday's barbecue?
options: The last kilo of 'vacío' (flank steak), four sausages ('chorizos'), and charcoal
Two chickens, potatoes, and salad greens
Fish fillets, lemons, and white wine
Pork ribs and a dozen empanadas
questions.explanation: Martín spots 'el último kilo de vacío' and Flor tells him to grab 'cuatro chorizos criollos y una bolsa grande de carbón.'

questions.question: How much does the butcher shop order cost in total?
questions.explanation: Martín says: 'el carnicero dice que son doce mil mangos en total' (12,000 pesos total).

questions.question: How do they divide the expenses for the barbecue?
options: Martín pays for the meat/charcoal, and Flor buys the red wine, bread, and tomatoes next door
Flor pays for everything with her credit card
They ask their friends to transfer money first
They decide to eat at a restaurant instead
questions.explanation: Martín asks Flor to buy the red wine, French bread, and tomatoes next door while he pays the butcher.

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: In Argentina, what do '¡Qué joya!', 'doce mil mangos', and 're copado' mean?
options: 'Qué joya' = Fantastic!; 'mangos' = pesos/bucks; 're copado' = super cool
'Qué joya' = How expensive!; 'mangos' = tropical fruit; 're copado' = too crowded
'Qué joya' = What a ring!; 'mangos' = coins; 're copado' = burnt on the grill
'Qué joya' = Hurry up!; 'mangos' = grams; 're copado' = very late
questions.explanation: In Argentine Spanish, '¡Qué joya!' is 'Fantastic!', 'mangos' means pesos/bucks, and 're copado' means super cool!
